topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Processor Gap
explanation: The processor-memory speed gap is mitigated by the memory hierarchy, a tiered system of storage (registers, L1/L2/L3 caches, main memory) ordered by decreasing speed and increasing capacity. Caching strategies minimize the average memory access time (AMAT) by exploiting locality of reference. Specifically, temporal locality keeps recently used data in faster cache levels, while spatial locality prefetches adjacent data blocks. Effective cache management ensures high hit rates, moving data blocks closer to the CPU to sustain high instruction throughput.
